newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hard to procure intervention funds from mkt--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Hard to procure intervention funds from mkt--MOF.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the International Finance Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (MOF), said on Wednesday it would be difficult to procure funds for foreign exchange intervention directly from the money market.

Currently, most of the funds for intervention are procured through the issuing of special foreign exchange bills, called financing bills (FBs), that have been mostly underwritten by the Bank of Japan (BOJ).
"If (the Ministry of Finance) procures intervention funds from the money market, that would send a signal that intervention is on its way," Sakakibara said.

FBs usually carry interest rates that are lower than prevailing market rates and are not always in great demand in the market, and the BOJ is obligated to buy most of the issues that are left unsold in the market.
For decades, the BOJ has been proposing that the 60-day government paper should be designed for sale in the market, instead of the central bank buying most of the issue amount.
The BOJ argues that if FBs were saleable in the market, this would undoubtedly add to money market liquidity and the globalisation of the Tokyo financial market.

But Sakakibara said: "It's common among other nations that intervention funds are raised via central banks and the treasury account... Thus it would be extremely difficult to raise funds from the market."
Sakakibara was speaking at a parliamentary finance committee meeting.
Helped by easy access to the intervention fund, Japan has in the past spent massively to exert influence on dollar/yen exchange rates.

Senior BOJ officials have said history shows that government financial dependence on a central bank that can print money without any limitations has caused hyperinflation that has ultimately ruined nations.
The FB rate is now at 0.375 percent or 0.125 percentage point below the discount rate, which currently stands at a record low 0.5 percent.
The outstanding volume of FBs totalled 29.835 trillion yen at the end of April.
The MOF and the Bank of Japan have been meeting since March to discuss the money market, including the contentious issue of FB underwriting by the BOJ.
